title: packet-bthci_evt: CS: fix empty step data and 15bit bugs
description:
According to Core Specification 6.0, Frequency_Compensation
and Measured_Freq_Offset fields use 15-big signed integer
format with the following range:
-100 ppm (0x58F0) to +100 ppm (0x2710).
The commit fixes format of printing negative values by
setting 16-th bit

According to Core Specification 6.0, Step_Data_Length[i]
can be 0. It can be the case when step was aborted, and
a Controller reports only step numbers and step channels
to the Host but doesn't provide any Mode_Role_Specific_Info.
The commit adds additional check of Step_Data_Length
before parsing fields in the Mode_Role_Specific_Info.

Signed-off-by: Ivan Iushkov <ivan.iushkov@nordicsemi.no>

notes.body: Not sure if it makes sense to ask here or if I should send an email to wireshark mailing list, but maybe someone from maintainers can help me to understand what's the release process, and when the changes made in this PR (and also the following PRs: [1](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/17580), [2](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18870), [3](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18892), [4](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18490), [5](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18516), [6](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18995)) will be available in wireshark releases? Should it be part of Wireshark 5 release, or there is also possibility of having it in Wireshark 4.x?

Hi Ivan,

The policy is easy, we only backport bug fix. for "new" feature, it is available on next major release

We can skip/forget to backport a fix, you can ask on PR/MR

you can use/try nighty build if you want/need https://www.wireshark.org/download/automated/
